lines.text: Open a Word or Markdown document, and Explainrig makes a best guess at the video: the scenes, the layouts, and a first draft of the narration.
You check every scene, fix what the guess got wrong, and approve it.
Then Showrig renders the video right on your own computer.

dropped.name: How the guess works
dropped.text: How the guess works Sections come from headings. When a document has none, bold list items and bold lines such as "Background:" mark them instead. The document type is scored from what is in it: dates and change words for a change notice, numbered instructions for a procedure, questions for an FAQ. The Why panel shows the scores. Each type has a recipe. A change notice gets a timeline, one scene per group of readers, and a call to action. A procedure gets one scene per step and a checklist. Narration drafts are the document's own sentences, rewritten into the second person ("Users with X are already set up" becomes "If you already use X, you're all set"). Pronunciations spell out acronyms, read web addresses with "dot", and expand short month names. You can change any of them. Left-out sections such as Background and Purpose wait in the Dropped panel, ready to restore.

dropped.name: Commands
dropped.text:
Commands Everything the window does is also a command. explainrig help lists them all: explainrig [DOC|PROJECT]        open the review window
explainrig doctor               check Showrig and its capture and voice setup
explainrig import DOC           make a project from the rules' best guess
explainrig show PROJECT         the storyboard as text
explainrig approve PROJECT      approve scenes (--all for every scene)
explainrig prepare PROJECT      voice and exact timings, then a timed preview
explainrig render PROJECT       the final video
explainrig auto DOC             import, approve, prepare and render in one go Build commands come from ~/.config/explainrig/config.json, so a machine that renders on another computer only needs different commands. contrib/srw-runner.sh is an example that renders on a Showrig worker over SSH.

dropped.name: Building
dropped.text: Building Explainrig is a Rust workspace. Build it with cargo build --release; the program is target/release/explainrig. Crate · Job · crates/doc · reads .docx and Markdown into ordered blocks · crates/guess · the rules: sections, document type, recipes, drafts, pronunciations · crates/film · writes the Showrig storyboard, the animated pages and the preview · crates/runner · checks prerequisites and runs Showrig · apps/explainrig · the window and the commands The test documents in tests/fixtures are made by tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py.
